transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-14 16:00 PT
- Duration: ~56 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood SE), Aisha (StrataForms HoML), Mark (CTO), Ben (Platform), Lina (Data Eng)

Summary:
Short discovery focused on where embeddings/rerank should run (hosted vs dedicated vs private), tradeoffs around fanout to vector DBs vs hybrid rerank, throughput SLAs and dimensionality/cost tradeoffs. Customer wanted concrete next steps: sandbox performance tests and security docs.

Topics discussed:
- Current infra + pain points
- Query fanout patterns and expected qps
- Embedding dims and cost tradeoffs
- Rerank architecture (in service vs in model)
- Hosting options: Redwood Hosted, Dedicated reserved pools, Private VPC/on-prem
- Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
- Benchmarks and smoke tests

Action items (captured in metadata above).

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey all, thanks for joining, uh, we'll do quick intros. I'm Sofia, AE at Redwood. Daniel and Maya from engineering will help on the deeper stuff. Aisha, Mark, Ben, Lina from StrataForms
[00:22] Aisha: Thanks, yeah, we really want to understand where to put embeddings compute, we currently use an in-house microservice that calls OpenAI for embeddings but cost is through the roof and latencies vary. We're exploring a move to self-hosted vectors with rerank to reduce downstream calls.
[00:40] Daniel: Got it, are you planning to batch or real time queries? Like, what's your qps and tail latency budget?
[00:52] Ben: Typical is 600 qps peak, 200 sustained, but a few customers spike up to ~2k for short bursts. We need 95th percentile < 150ms for search UX, ideally sub-100ms for typeahead flows.
[01:10] Sofia: Okay that helps. Two broad patterns we see: 1) embed at ingest and fanout to vector DB for fast nearest-neighbors then rerank with a small model — low latency but more VDB ops; 2) do hybrid where candidate retrieval is co-located or cached in runtime and rerank happens with hosted model calls — fewer VDB calls but higher per-request compute.
[01:36] Aisha: For rerank, are teams typically doing cross-encoder reranks on-prem or from hosted? We have data residency constraints for some enterprise customers.
[01:48] Maya: Many customers start with Hosted for faster time-to-value then migrate to Dedicated or Private when they need isolation or predictable throughput. Cross-encoders are heavier — you can run them on Dedicated GPUs with batching to get cost-effective throughput. Private gives you full control for data residency + KMS.
[02:12] Mark: Our security team will want KMS/HSM and SSO integration. Also audit logs accessible to our SIEM. Is that all available with Private?
[02:24] Daniel: Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS, SAML/SSO, and audit log shipping. Dedicated has isolated capacity but the control plane is still managed — we can ship logs and integrate with your SIEM but KMS is more limited than full Private.
[02:44] Lina: On dimensionality — we've seen 1536 dims are common, but we were considering compacting to 256 or 512 to save index size. Any impact on rerank quality?
[02:56] Sofia: There's a tradeoff. Lower dims reduce index storage and VDB fanout cost, but retrieval quality can drop for fine-grained semantics. Typical pattern: use 768 or 1024 for balance, then rerank with higher-fidelity cross-encoder to recover precision. Also consider hybrid approaches with metadata filtering.
[03:18] Ben: Do you have guidance on embedding model choices vs dims? We use OpenAI ada embeddings now, thinking about open models.
[03:28] Maya: We publish model profiles; for production we often recommend a vetted open model at 1024 dims for similarity retrieval, and then a smaller cross-encoder at inference time for rerank (or a quantized variant on Dedicated). We'll share our model-performance sheet.
[03:44] Aisha: Throughput—if we run cross-encoder rerank on Dedicated, what throughput can we expect per GPU? Our goal is 2k qps bursts with rerank top-50.
[03:56] Daniel: Reranking top-50 with a ~3B cross-encoder quantized on Ampere A100 style nodes, with batching and optimized kernels, you can push several hundred qps per GPU for rerank. For 2k burst, we suggest autoscaled Dedicated pool or mixed routing where cheap candidate retrieval reduces rerank frequency. Also prefix/KV cache for repeated queries helps.
[04:24] Mark: Can Redwood route to a cheaper model when under load? We want graceful degradation.
[04:30] Sofia: Yes, smart routing policies allow fallback to smaller models or other regions. You configure policies: latency SLO-first or cost-first. In Hosted we provide automatic fallbacks; in Dedicated you configure fallbacks within your pool.
[04:44] Ben: For indexing, we're using Milvus ATM. How does Redwood integrate — do you need VPC peering, or do you recommend co-locating vectors?
[04:56] Maya: Integration patterns: 1) VDB external via VPC peering (typical) where Redwood calls your Milvus cluster; 2) Index-in-cloud where you host vectors in a managed VDB partner; 3) Edge caching with periodic sync. For latency sensitive paths co-locating or using a read-replica near the inference nodes reduces fanout latency. We'll share an integration playbook.
[05:20] Aisha: If we do peering, is there egress cost from Redwood calls?
[05:26] Daniel: Network charges depend on cloud setup; with Private deploy it's in your VPC so traffic stays internal. Hosted implies standard outbound calls from our managed infra which can incur egress depending on cloud region — we'll include cost considerations in the spreadsheet.
[05:42] Mark: We need deterministic cost model for budgeting, especially for large index ops. Any tooling?
[05:49] Sofia: Redwood Optimize suggests batching/quantization profiles per workload and provides per-token and per-rerank cost breakouts. We'll include sample unit economics for your qps and top-k.
[06:02] Lina: For fanout to vector DB, at 600 qps with top-100 fanout we'd be doing 60k vector ops per sec — that seems huge. How do folks reduce that?
[06:14] Daniel: Common strategies: reduce top-k candidate size (top-50 or top-20), use two-stage retrieval (metadata filters then sparse retrieval), precompute hot-item caches, and use compressed or lower-dim embeddings. Also asynchronous background refresh for cold items.
[06:34] Aisha: What about hybrid search — combining lexical + vector? We have many exact-match queries too.
[06:41] Maya: Hybrid search is very common. You can do lexical filters in DB then vector re-rank, or score blend at retrieval. For throughput, doing lexical prefiltering reduces vector fanout dramatically.
[06:54] Ben: On the Dedicated sizing — how do we size GPU pools for both embeddings at ingest and rerank peaks?
[07:02] Daniel: We recommend separating workloads: CPU-backed ingest pipelines that compute embeddings in batch, and GPU-backed Dedicated pool for rerank and heavy on-demand tasks. Sizing starts from expected peak rerank qps and batching efficiency; we'll run a sizing workshop with your telemetry to estimate GPUs needed.
[07:22] Mark: How long to spin up a Dedicated pool for a POC? We want to run a 2-week pilot with realistic traffic.
[07:29] Sofia: We can provision a sandbox Dedicated pool in ~5 business days with reserved configs and demo workloads; Private will take longer due to network setup and KMS—typically 2-4 weeks depending on your infra team.
[07:44] Aisha: For evaluation, can Redwood run a smoke test hitting our Milvus instance and measure end-to-end tail latency?
[07:52] Daniel: Yes — Daniel: we can run a 10k queries/s scaled test in the sandbox against your VDB if you provide sample dataset or a mocked endpoint. We'll need your query distribution and a service account for access.
[08:06] Lina: On the security side, will audit events include token-level traces? Our compliance needs it.
[08:12] Maya: We provide request-level tracing and audit logs with metadata: model used, route, latency. In Private you get the most complete controls. Hosted provides masked logs for privacy.
[08:24] Mark: Any caveats with quantization for cross-encoders? We worry accuracy regressions.
[08:30] Daniel: Quantization can drop quality but often minimal with careful calibration. Redwood Optimize can run A/B tests across quantized and float variants and watch MRR or downstream metrics. We'll help set up evals and regressions alerts.
[08:46] Aisha: Do you have any customers with similar scale and constraints?
[08:50] Sofia: Yes, a retail search company with similar qps uses Dedicated for rerank and host vectors in Milvus with peering; they run a hybrid (lexical+vector) and use smaller top-k with cross-encoder rerank for final scoring. We can anonymize the case study.
[09:04] Ben: What about cost delta between 1024 and 512 dims at our index size (30M vectors)?
[09:12] Maya: Rough numbers — 30M @1024 is roughly double the storage of 512; indexing and fanout costs scale similarly. We'll put exact storage and egress numbers in the cost model.
[09:26] Mark: For the pilot success criteria: we need sub-150ms 95th p99? sorry p95 <150ms on search surface, rerank recall lift of +8-10% vs baseline, and predictable monthly cost within 10%.
[09:39] Sofia: Great, we'll align on that and design the pilot accordingly.
[09:46] Aisha: Anything else from your side?
[09:49] Daniel: One note — if you care about on-prem, we have an air-gapped package but it'll add ops overhead; we'll scope that if needed.
[09:58] Lina: We'll prepare the query distribution and sample data.
[10:02] Sofia: Perfect. We'll send the spreadsheet and SOC2 docs, spin up a sandbox for the Dedicated smoke test, and schedule the security deep dive.
[10:12] Mark: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

Recap / Next steps:
- Redwood: send hosting options + cost model spreadsheet (Sofia)
